title: Family History of Pancreatic Cancer: Genetic Risk and Who Needs Surveillance
description: Why average-risk people do not need pancreatic cancer blood-test screening and how selected high-risk families may qualify for MRI/EUS surveillance.

faq.question: Can CA 19-9 screen people with family history?
faq.answer: Not reliably. Selected high-risk people need specialist risk assessment and an imaging surveillance pathway.

faq.question: Does one affected relative always mean surveillance?
faq.answer: Not necessarily. Gene status, number and relationship of affected relatives and age at diagnosis affect eligibility.

faq.question: Should relatives undergo genetic counselling?
faq.answer: Genetic counselling is useful when family history or known inherited variants suggest a hereditary syndrome.
